Steadily getting worse? Gosh, I don't know if I'd say worse and worse. I mean, it's definitely been a nuisance since then, but I think it's mostly just stayed about the same level of bad since the scare. It's just so frustrating, you know? Not being able to rely on my own head. 

It reminds me of this old pocket watch my grandfather gave me. Beautiful thing, gold plated, had his initials engraved on the back. E.J.H. Edward James Harrison. He was a watchmaker, actually. Concentrating? Yeah, actually, that's been... well, it's definitely been tricky. Apple, table, coin. Got it. Apple... you know, we used to have an apple tree in the backyard of the house I grew up in. A big old Macintosh tree. Hmm, I don't know if she's said it's gotten worse exactly. She gets annoyed when I forget things, sure, but I don't know about worse. Like yesterday, she sent me to the hardware store for some special potting soil she likes, and I came back with birdseed instead. She’s got this whole garden setup in the backyard now. Planted all these hydrangeas along the back fence. \n\nDid you know they change color depending on what's in the dirt? You can put old coffee grounds in there to make the flowers blue. Or maybe it makes them pink, I can never remember. We save all our coffee grounds in this little tin can by the sink. It’s an old Maxwell House can, the metal kind, you know? My dad used to keep his fishing worms in a can just like that. We'd go out to Miller's Pond every Sunday when I was a kid... caught a largemouth bass as big as my arm out there once. Fought like crazy. Broke my favorite rod, actually. \n\nBut anyway, what was I saying? Oh, my wife. Yeah, she complains about me forgetting the groceries or the tools or the appointments, but I honestly couldn't tell you if she thinks it's worse now than it was a year ago. She's always got something to say about my listening skills, so it all kind of blends together.\n\nDoctor: Besides forgetting things, have you noticed any new difficulty with tasks like managing your finances, following instructions, or finding your way in places you know well?\n\nPatient: Finances and instructions? Well, I wouldn't say I'm getting lost or anything like that. I know my way around town just fine. I've lived here for... gosh, going on forty years now. We bought the house back in '84, right before the big blizzard. I tell you, I've never seen snow like that since. It was piled up all the way to the gutters! We had this old snowblower, a Toro I think, and it just choked on the stuff. Had to shovel the whole driveway by hand. My back was out for a week. \n\nBut, uh, paying bills and things? No, I haven't noticed any new trouble with that. I mean, my wife usually handles the checkbook anyway. She's got this whole system with color-coded folders. Red for utilities, blue for medical, green for the house stuff. She tried to explain it to me once, but honestly, I just let her do it. She used to work as a bookkeeper for a small shipping company downtown, so she's good with numbers. They shipped mostly auto parts, I think. Or maybe it was farm equipment? I remember she brought home this giant calendar once with all these tractors on it. I hung it up in the garage for years.\n\nSo, yeah, no new problems with that kind of stuff, really.
